alloy.preparation: Supplied as hot-forged 18-mm-diameter rods. Tested in the as-received hot-forged condition. Cut from rods, epoxy-mounted to expose about 0.8 cm², coarse-ground with SiC paper and fine-ground with alumina paste.
alloy.microstructure: Martensite with some δ-ferrite inclusions at former austenite grain boundaries. Small carbide particles, presumed M23C6, detected in all specimens. Fine carbide precipitates described at γ–δ boundaries and within δ phase in hot-forged specimens.

test_method.procedure_description: Stepwise anodic polarization at 25°C; experimental text specifies 50 mV per 30 s. Potential plotted on the H scale. Figure 5 supplies separate hot-forged/open and 1050°C-water-quenched/filled symbols for each NaCl concentration. Optical microscopy, XRD and electron microprobe support the phase/context discussion.
test_method.pitting_criterion: Potential of pit nucleation E′np from anodic polarization. Upward square markers in Figure 5 explicitly denote no pitting, represented as lower limits.

experiments.result_note: Approximate graphical potential of pit nucleation E′np. Connecting lines do not create observations. Separate forged and quenched outcomes retained even when they overlap. Table 1 gives composition in % without an explicit mass/atomic basis. Figure 1 displays a conflicting “50 mV/sec” label, while the experimental method and Figure 2 specify 50 mV/30 sec; the stepwise method is retained without calculating a sweep rate.

alloy.preparation: Supplied as hot-forged 18-mm-diameter rods. Heated in air at 1050°C and water-quenched; paper identifies most electrochemical tests as using a 1-h heating period. Cut from rods, epoxy-mounted to expose about 0.8 cm², coarse-ground with SiC paper and fine-ground with alumina paste.
alloy.microstructure: Martensite with some δ-ferrite inclusions at former austenite grain boundaries. Small carbide particles, presumed M23C6, detected in all specimens. Quenching did not essentially change phase composition; it increased homogeneity of δ/γ phases and made δ grains somewhat larger and rounder.

alloy.microstructure: Austenite and ferrite; no σ phase detected. The 10% Mn heat contains more δ-ferrite than the 9.6% Mn heat. Small carbide particles, presumed M23C6, detected in all specimens. Quenching did not essentially change phase composition; it increased homogeneity of δ/γ phases and made δ grains somewhat larger and rounder.

test_method.procedure_description: Stepwise anodic polarization at 25°C; experimental text specifies 50 mV per 30 s. Potential plotted on the H scale. Figure 5 supplies separate hot-forged/open and 1050°C-water-quenched/filled symbols for each NaCl concentration. Optical microscopy, XRD and electron microprobe support the phase/context discussion.
test_method.pitting_criterion: Potential of pit nucleation E′np from anodic polarization. Upward square markers in Figure 5 explicitly denote no pitting, represented as lower limits.

experiments.result_note: Approximate graphical potential of pit nucleation E′np. Connecting lines do not create observations. Separate forged and quenched outcomes retained even when they overlap. Table 1 gives composition in % without an explicit mass/atomic basis. Figure 1 displays a conflicting “50 mV/sec” label, while the experimental method and Figure 2 specify 50 mV/30 sec; the stepwise method is retained without calculating a sweep rate. Carbon for this 10.0% Mn heat is printed n.d.; its amount is null rather than borrowed from the distinct 9.6% Mn heat.
